hook: Jerome Powell chaired the US Federal Reserve through the post-pandemic inflation cycle and the emergence of AI-driven capital spending as a factor in the US economy, before his term as Chair ended in May 2026.
name: Jerome Powell

quote.text: I don't think interest rates are an important part of the AI data center story. People think there are great economics in building these data centers, and they're making a lot of money building them.
quote.context: Jerome Powell, FOMC press conference, October 29, 2025

moniker: Former Chair of the US Federal Reserve

reading.body:
Powell's assessment of data center economics explicitly separates infrastructure investment returns from interest rate policy, suggesting the AI capital buildout is self-funding on fundamentals rather than dependent on monetary accommodation.

This statement matters because it came from the chair of the institution most capable of constraining AI infrastructure growth through cost of capital. Powell led the Federal Reserve through both the post-pandemic inflation cycle and the period when AI-driven data center demand became measurable in national accounts. His October 2025 framing indicates the Fed's chief policymaker saw the data center buildout as economically rational independent of interest rates. That distinction suggests capital will continue flowing to compute infrastructure regardless of monetary policy shifts.

For AI scaling specifically, this decouples infrastructure from the usual vulnerability to central bank tightening. If data center construction returns are attractive on their own terms, rate hikes constrain the sector less than they would a traditional leverage-driven investment bubble. Powell's tenure ended May 2026, before the full scale of grid constraints became binding. His quoted position reflected the period when electricity and buildings were emerging as the actual limiting factors on compute deployment, not cost of capital.

quick_facts: Served as Chair of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors from February 5, 2018 to May 22, 2026
Confirmed by the Senate to a second term as Chair in May 2022 and sworn in May 23, 2022
Named chair pro tempore on May 15, 2026 pending the swearing-in of successor Kevin Warsh
Succeeded as Fed Chair by Kevin Warsh, sworn in May 22, 2026
Separately holds a Board of Governors term set to run until January 31, 2028
